newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Kidnapped oil executive freed in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped oil executive freed in Colombia.

text.p: A senior Colombian oil official has been released by leftist guerrilla kidnappers after 16 months in captivity, following payment of a ransom.
Alfonso Manrique, a member of the board of directors of the state oil company Ecopetrol, was taken by gunmen who burst into his office in downtown Bogota in November 1995.

In an interview on Monday with the Radionet news programme, Manrique identified his kidnappers as Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels and said he was freed on Sunday in exchange for an unspecified ransom.
Manrique and Alberto Villamizar, head of the government's anti-kidnapping office, refused to say how much ransom was paid for the oil executive's freedom.
Manrique, clearly overjoyed at being set free, said: "The important thing is that I've been liberated."
The FARC, Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla group, specialises in kidnapping and the protection of rural drug operations.
Roughly half of all kidnappings in Colombia, a country Villamizar says has the world's highest abduction rate, are blamed on leftist guerrillas.
